s: Distributed commit log supporting durable pub/sub, stream processing, and event sourcing with partition-level ordering.
w: Producers write to topic partitions distributed across brokers; consumers in groups each own partitions ensuring parallel processing without duplication. Replication factor controls durability (ISR consensus). Consumer offsets track progress; retention is time/size-based. Kafka Connect integrates databases/files; Kafka Streams enables exactly-once processing within the cluster. Log compaction keeps latest value per key for state topics.
use: Event backbone connecting dozens of microservices via pub/sub
Stream processing input (Flink, Spark Streaming, Kafka Streams)
Decoupling producers and consumers at massive throughput
Audit log / event sourcing store with durable ordered history
CDC destination receiving Debezium database change streams
avoid: Simple task queue where SQS/RabbitMQ is simpler and cheaper
Low-volume systems where operational overhead of Kafka cluster is unjustified
Request-reply patterns (Kafka is fire-and-forget; use gRPC for sync)

props.replication_factor: Copies of each partition across brokers (typically 3)
props.retention_ms: How long messages persist before deletion

pat.d: Kafka IS the event store: append-only log becomes system of record.
Kafka topics -> consumers build read models in elasticsearch/redis.

pits: Consumer lag spiraling silently - monitor lag per group per topic and alert on growth
Partition hot-spots from poor key design - use high-cardinality keys for even distribution
Rebalancing storms when consumers join/leave frequently - static membership reduces churn
tips: At-least-once is the default; exactly-once requires idempotent producers + transactional consumers
Consumer group model is the interview essential: one partition consumed by exactly one consumer in a group
